name: Egyptian woven linen from Hatshepsut’s storehouses
description: Egyptian weavers made linen by interlacing fine flax threads; a sheet recovered at Thebes preserves warp and weft selvages and ancient repairs.

date.label: Approximately 1491–1473 BCE
date.basis: The source reports the date for this scoped event or archaeological context.

events.statement: A surviving fine linen sheet is dated by the museum to approximately 1491–1473 BCE.

evidence.supports: A surviving fine linen sheet is dated by the museum to approximately 1491–1473 BCE.
The source attributes this contribution to Egyptian linen weavers.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated case currently researched, not a claim of the capability’s original invention or global priority.

caveats: The museum’s dating applies to the object or its context, not a demonstrated invention date or a particular loom design.

research.note: Independent review checked the Met object catalogue and dimensions. This surviving cloth is an instance of weaving, not evidence for its invention or global origin.

measures.subject: Surviving linen sheet
measures.conditions: Museum reports greatest length; an object dimension, not total workshop output.
